observations.contract: Global grip frame loses rotation and parent
observations.trace: For a hypothetical recipe with no implicit shaft, a positive Grip of length0.1 m and id handle is attached at weapon.root with a +90-degree Z rotation and Grip role. Registration creates both handle.top and grip.top at approximately [-0.1,0,0], but stores the rotation under handle only. A later Box attached to grip.top at Origin with overlap0.01 derives owner grip from the alias text, finds no grip rotation and uses zero rotation, yielding an offset approximately [-0.1,-0.01,0]. The same point addressed as handle.top uses the handle rotation and overlap toward approximately [-0.09,0,0]. For grip.top, attachment_contact finds neither a component named grip nor an implicit shaft and returns before parent-bound checks.
observations.remaining: Symbolic source-level reasoning only; no recipe, model, bounds check, panic or gameplay ran. The direct handle path may independently pass or fail physical contact; no such result is asserted. Historical Adler335 first recorded the same alias/parent family with scoped future source rereads; normal authored use and global aliases remain open.

observations.trace: With an invalid holder wall-thickness parameter, holder_identity returns a typed ValidationError::Holder("parameters") vector and HolderConstruction maps it to GenerateError::Invalid. Its Display text is only invalid weapon design; validate_holder and derive_holder_properties convert the error to that text and place it in ValidationError::Construction. Separately, Construction::new formats typed RecipeError into String before public generate_model and downstream consumers. Blade sampling, geometry and allocation return further separate String reasons.
observations.remaining: No invalid holder, display formatting, constructor, codec or test ran. Holder invalid-vector erasure and general construction-error ownership are distinct existing historical records, even if they share a connected error-design repair. Preserve actual native causes and intentional classifications; complete alias review remains open.

observations.trace: BladeProfile::validate requires Recessed exactly when fuller is present before the blade section path unwraps fuller. Feature-station refinement samples quarter, midpoint and three-quarter deviations, rejects at the f64 mantissa-depth limit, and applies construction_budget before adding accepted stations. Groove transition refinement has finitely many cutoffs, and its failing interval without an interior cutoff returns the prior error. The separate adaptive_curve recursion previously reviewed has different depth-limit semantics.
observations.remaining: Guarded unwrap remains a repository style concern but no ordinary missing-fuller panic is established. Sampled normal/error checks do not independently prove every continuous geometry bound for arbitrary producer callbacks. No geometry or test ran; actual supported forms and precision contracts remain open.

observations.trace: holder_part receives a crease argument, and callers supply0.82 for sheath pieces and0.65 for suspension/loop pieces, but the parameter is named _crease and unused. PartSource::new instead sets smoothing_cosine=0.25. ModelPart::from_source uses the resulting cosine when deciding whether same-group neighboring normals can share a vertex; for a hypothetical pair with normal dot0.5, 0.25 and0.82 make different comparisons.
observations.remaining: No holder, model, mesh, normal, image or test ran. It remains a policy question whether the passed crease values were intended to control smoothing and whether actual admitted holder meshes contain an affected normal pair. Do not assert an observed visual regression or merge this question with physical geometry.
